wholeQuestion.question: Which examination finding is most specific in documentation?

wholeQuestion.question: Why should muscle findings be compared with baseline habitus when possible?
choices: Age, training, disability, and chronic disease can affect expected muscle stores
Muscle anatomy is identical in every patient
Baseline eliminates the need for history

choiceReview.choice: Age, training, disability, and chronic disease can affect expected muscle stores
choiceReview.assessment: Interpret expected tissue in the context of prior habitus, age, activity, disability and disease; training is contextual history, not a new diagnostic cutoff.

choiceReview.choice: Muscle anatomy is identical in every patient
choiceReview.assessment: Patients do not have identical baseline muscle stores.

choiceReview.choice: Baseline eliminates the need for history
choiceReview.assessment: Baseline comparison still requires history and clinical context.

wholeQuestion.question: Which competing cause should be considered when interpreting reduced handgrip strength?

choiceReview.assessment: Painful arthritis is a competing musculoskeletal contributor to reduced performance. The cohort supports clinical context, not a nutrition-independent causal estimate.

A serum chloride value alone does not identify the competing musculoskeletal cause.

choiceReview.choice: As direct proof of adequate protein intake
choiceReview.assessment: Edema does not establish adequate protein intake.

wholeQuestion.question: What is the best response to visible muscle loss after a focal neurologic injury?

choiceReview.assessment: Denervation and disuse can cause focal muscle loss despite adequate intake, so assess the competing neurologic cause.

Albumin does not establish tissue loss or its cause.

wholeLesson.title: Physical and Functional Assessment
wholeLesson.summary: The bedside examination turns suspected tissue loss into observable evidence and helps distinguish fat, muscle, fluid, and function.
wholeLesson.application: Compare bilateral sites when appropriate, consider age and baseline habitus, and document the location and degree of loss rather than writing a vague global impression.

lesson.heading: Inspect specific tissue compartments
lesson.body: Nutrition focused examination evaluates fat stores, muscle groups, fluid accumulation, oral and skin findings, and functional clues. Findings should be interpreted with the history because immobility, denervation, aging, trauma, and organ disease can alter muscle independently of intake.

lesson.heading: Treat function as context
lesson.body: A decline in grip, mobility, transfers, or usual activity can support the assessment, but function is affected by pain, cognition, neurologic disease, sedation, and acute illness. It should not be treated as a nutrition specific measurement in isolation.

keyPoints: Name the anatomical site and tissue examined.
Account for nonnutrition causes of weakness or atrophy.
Use repeated findings to monitor trajectory when the method is consistent.

check.question: Why should reduced handgrip strength not be interpreted alone as proof of malnutrition?
choices: Pain, neurologic disease, sedation, and acute illness can also reduce performance
Grip strength measures only body fat
Grip strength is never clinically useful
It directly measures serum protein concentration
check.rationale: Functional measures are clinically useful but nonspecific and require interpretation within the complete assessment.

lessonReview.summaryAndApplication: Specific observed tissue and fluid findings must be integrated with baseline and clinical context; these are documentation principles, not new severity thresholds.
lessonReview.body1: Academy/ASPEN2012 native4-7 supports fat, muscle, fluid, oral/skin findings and competing denervation/disuse causes; ICUweakness2020 native1/2 supports illness context.
lessonReview.body2: ICUweakness2020 native4/5 supports volitional-testing and functional limitations; RA2023 native2/3/7 supports pain/joint context without a causal nutrition claim.
lessonReview.keyPoints: Defined sites and consistent examination with documented context support interpretation of trajectory.
checkChoiceReviews: Clinical factors can reduce or prevent valid volitional performance.
Grip does not measure only fat.
Grip can contribute useful contextual information.
Grip does not directly measure serum protein.
